description: Proof-artifact taxonomy for the ft-tf6g3 reality-check epic. Categories 1-10 are the bridge-plan core taxonomy; category 11 is an extension already referenced by a later child bead.

categories.name: Type-Level Proof
categories.description: Compile-time proof encoded in Rust types, sealed traits, trait bounds, lint gates, or dependency bans.

categories.name: Property Test
categories.description: Generated-input test that asserts an invariant across many cases instead of one hand-picked fixture.

categories.name: Loom Concurrency Proof
categories.description: Systematic concurrency interleaving exploration for async or synchronization behavior.

categories.name: Conformance Artifact
categories.description: Golden, schema, protocol, contract, visual, or wire-format check against an explicit expected shape.

categories.name: Quantitative Attestation
categories.description: Measured result with machine-readable parameters, sample counts, thresholds, and provenance.

categories.name: Formal Method
categories.description: Explicit model, theorem, state-machine proof, or model-checking artifact with a verifiable invariant.

categories.name: Information-Theoretic Bound
categories.description: Entropy, leakage, distinguishability, or recall/precision bound with stated assumptions and data.

categories.name: Network Calculus Bound
categories.description: Queueing, Lindley recursion, min-plus, arrival/service-curve, or tail-bound analysis for resource claims.

categories.name: Differential Comparison
categories.description: Comparison against another implementation, oracle, previous release, or independent backend.

categories.name: Cryptographic Attestation
categories.description: Signature, content-addressed manifest, hash chain, transparency-log, or provenance proof.

categories.name: Topological Invariant
categories.description: Graph, topology, reachability, cut-set, packing, or persistent-homology invariant that proves structural behavior beyond the core ten categories.

non_proof_classifications.description: Implementation or infrastructure that enables a future proof artifact but is not itself a proof.
Governance, cadence, release, or review discipline that routes proof work without asserting a technical property.
Tooling, CI, runner, mirror, or operational support needed to execute proof work.
Bead graph, ownership, scheduling, or cross-agent routing work.
